events.reason: Ascending colon adenocarcinoma with liver lesions

documents.title: Oncology Consultation
documents.author: oncology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE MEDICAL ONCOLOGY - INITIAL CONSULTATION
Visit date: 01/06/2025
Patient: Carl Clark, DOB 09/28/1952 (72 y)
Referred by: gastroenterology. cc: primary care

HPI: Mr. Clark is a 72-year-old man with type 2 diabetes, hypertension and hyperlipidemia who was recently worked up by GI for a colorectal neoplasm. Over roughly three months he has had a right upper quadrant pain that comes and goes, and he has lost about 10 pounds without trying. Colonoscopy 11/21/2024 showed an ascending colon mass; biopsy invasive adenocarcinoma, moderately differentiated. CT abdomen 11/12/2024 showed multiple bilobar liver lesions, largest 4.6 cm.

Liver core biopsy (IR, 12/19/2024): metastatic adenocarcinoma. Immunostains CK20 positive, CDX2 positive, CK7 negative, consistent with colorectal origin.

Medications: metformin, lisinopril, aspirin 81 mg daily.
Allergies: NKDA.
FH: father - colon cancer at 70 (deceased). Mother - T2DM, HTN.
SH: retired postal worker. Never smoker. No alcohol. Lives with his wife.

Vitals: within normal limits.
Exam: Alert, thin, ECOG 1. No jaundice. Firm, enlarged liver. No ascites. No lymphadenopathy. Heart and lungs unremarkable.

Labs today: Hgb 12.8 g/dL, WBC 7,000/uL, platelets 250,000/uL. AST 68, ALT 55, alkaline phosphatase 210, total bilirubin 1.2. CEA 46.2 ng/mL.

Assessment: Adenocarcinoma of the ascending colon metastatic to the liver (secondary malignant neoplasm of liver). Bilobar disease is not resectable at present.

Plan:
1. Staging CT of chest, abdomen and pelvis with contrast - scheduled 1/14.
2. Surgical referral for right hemicolectomy to remove the primary, given the bulky mass and his symptoms.
3. Systemic chemotherapy after recovery from surgery; we will review regimen options at the next visit.
4. Case to be presented at tumor board.

We discussed the diagnosis and the goals of treatment at length with Mr. and Mrs. Clark.

Medical Oncology

results.text: Aerobic and anaerobic bottles positive at 2 days. Gram stain: gram-positive rods. Identification: Clostridium septicum.

reports.study: CT abdomen and pelvis with contrast
reports.text:
Comparison: CT abdomen 11/12/2024 and staging CT 01/14/2025.
Known irregular mass-like thickening of the ascending colon. Known multiple hypoattenuating liver lesions in both lobes, not significantly changed. No colonic diverticula or pericolonic inflammation to suggest diverticulitis. Small bowel and colon are normal in caliber; no obstruction. No free air. No abscess or drainable collection. No ascites. Gallbladder, pancreas, spleen and kidneys unremarkable. Bladder unremarkable.
reports.conclusion: No diverticulitis or bowel obstruction. Known ascending colon mass and liver metastases without significant interval change.

documents.title: Emergency Department Physician Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT
Date of service: 03/01/2025, 21:10
Patient: Carl Clark, 72 M

Chief complaint: abdominal pain, fever, confusion.

HPI: 72-year-old with T2DM, HTN, hyperlipidemia and colorectal cancer metastatic to the liver, brought in by his wife after two days of severe belly pain with fevers and new confusion. Per wife, no bowel movement in three days and he has refused food because of the pain. Hemicolectomy was planned for later this month.

PMH: as above. PSH: tonsillectomy, knee arthroscopy.
Meds: metformin 1000 mg BID, lisinopril 20 mg daily, aspirin 81 mg daily.
Allergies: NKDA.
Social: never smoker, no alcohol, retired postal worker.

Triage vitals: T 38.9 C (102 F), BP 90/60, HR 110, RR 22.

Exam: Ill appearing, intermittently confused, oriented to self and place. Tachycardic, regular. Lungs clear. Abdomen diffusely tender to palpation, no rebound, no guarding. No rash.

Labs: notable for leukocytosis with a left shift.
Blood cultures x2 drawn before antibiotics.

CT abdomen/pelvis with IV contrast: no diverticulitis, no bowel obstruction; known colon mass and liver lesions unchanged.

ED course: 30 mL/kg crystalloid with improvement in BP. Broad-spectrum antibiotics started: piperacillin-tazobactam and vancomycin IV. Surgery and hospital medicine consulted.

Impression: sepsis, source not yet identified, in a patient with metastatic colon cancer.
Disposition: admitted to the surgical service with medicine co-management.

Addendum 03/03: blood cultures from 3/1 growing gram-positive rods; final identification Clostridium septicum. Vancomycin stopped; continuing piperacillin-tazobactam.

Emergency Medicine

events.reason: Sepsis with Clostridium septicum bacteremia; right hemicolectomy

medications.drug: amoxicillin 875 MG / clavulanate 125 MG Oral Tablet
medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth twice daily with food through 3/21
medications.reason: Complete treatment of Clostridium septicum bacteremia

reports.text: Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response, ventricular rate 110 bpm. No discernible P waves; irregularly irregular RR intervals. QRS narrow. LVH voltage. No acute ST elevation.
reports.conclusion: Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response, rate 110.

reports.text: Supine and upright views of the abdomen. Diffuse gas throughout mildly distended small and large bowel. No free air under the diaphragm. Surgical staples in the right abdomen. No abnormal calcification.
reports.conclusion: Diffuse bowel gas pattern compatible with postoperative ileus. No free intraperitoneal air.

reports.text:
Specimen: right colon and terminal ileum (right hemicolectomy).
Gross: segment of terminal ileum and right colon with an ulcerated mass in the ascending colon; tattoo ink present distal to the mass.
Microscopic: moderately differentiated adenocarcinoma invading through the muscularis propria into pericolic adipose tissue. Proximal, distal and radial margins free of tumor. Two of eighteen lymph nodes contain metastatic adenocarcinoma.
Pathologic stage: pT3 pN1b. Distant metastasis to liver per clinical history.
reports.conclusion: Ascending colon: moderately differentiated adenocarcinoma, pT3 pN1b (2/18 nodes), margins negative. Stage IV with known liver metastases.

procedures.procedure: Hospital discharge day management, 30 minutes or less

documents.title: Operative Report - Right Hemicolectomy
documents.author: general surgery
documents.body:
OPERATIVE REPORT
Date of surgery: 03/05/2025
Patient: Carl Clark, 72 M

Preoperative diagnosis: adenocarcinoma of the ascending colon with liver metastases; Clostridium septicum bacteremia, treated.
Postoperative diagnosis: same.
Procedure: open right hemicolectomy with primary ileocolic anastomosis.
Anesthesia: general endotracheal.

Indications: biopsy-proven ascending colon cancer, planned for resection of the primary, now admitted with C. septicum bacteremia from the tumor. After four days of IV antibiotics with defervescence and negative repeat cultures, resection was brought forward to this admission.

Findings: mass in the ascending colon, tattooed. Liver with known lesions, not addressed. No peritoneal deposits seen. No perforation.

Description: midline laparotomy. Right colon mobilized along the white line of Toldt; ileocolic pedicle ligated at its origin. Terminal ileum and transverse colon divided with staplers; stapled side-to-side ileocolic anastomosis, common enterotomy closed. Hemostasis. Fascia closed with running looped suture; skin stapled.

Intraoperative events: new atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response during mobilization, treated by anesthesia with IV metoprolol; hemodynamically stable throughout.

EBL 150 mL. Specimen to pathology. Disposition: PACU, then medical floor, stable.

General Surgery

documents.title: Hospital Discharge Summary
documents.author: general surgery
documents.body:
DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted: 03/01/2025 (via ED)   Discharged: 03/14/2025
Service: General Surgery, with hospital medicine co-management
PCP: primary care (copy sent)

Principal diagnosis: sepsis due to Clostridium septicum bacteremia, source colon adenocarcinoma.
Other diagnoses this admission: adenocarcinoma of the ascending colon with liver metastases, s/p open right hemicolectomy 3/5; postoperative atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response, resolved; postoperative ileus, resolved; type 2 diabetes; hypertension; hyperlipidemia.

Hospital course:
1. Sepsis / C. septicum bacteremia. Presented febrile, hypotensive and confused. Fluids and piperacillin-tazobactam plus vancomycin; cultures grew gram-positive rods on 3/3, identified as C. septicum; vancomycin stopped. Repeat cultures 3/4 no growth. Mental status back to baseline by 3/3. Completing therapy with oral amoxicillin-clavulanate through 3/21.

2. Colon cancer. Taken for open right hemicolectomy on 3/5 (see operative report). Pathology: moderately differentiated adenocarcinoma, pT3 pN1b, margins negative. Outpatient oncology to resume care and discuss chemotherapy.

3. Postoperative atrial fibrillation with RVR. AF began intraoperatively and was treated with IV metoprolol. He was asymptomatic overnight in normal rhythm by vitals (HR 78, BP 130/85). On the morning of POD 1 (3/6) he reported palpitations and mild shortness of breath; pulse irregularly irregular, BP 120/80; ECG atrial fibrillation, ventricular rate 110. Oral metoprolol tartrate for rate control. Converted to sinus rhythm 3/7 and remained in sinus on telemetry for the rest of the stay. Metoprolol was not continued at discharge.

4. Postoperative ileus. On POD 4 (3/9) abdominal distension with no flatus or stool since surgery; afebrile (37.2), BP 135/85, HR 88; abdomen distended and tympanic, nontender, bowel sounds sparse. Hgb 12.5, WBC 9.0, Na 140, K 4.2, Cl 102, HCO3 24, BUN 18, Cr 1.0. Abdominal films: diffuse bowel gas, no free air. Managed with bowel rest, NG decompression, IV fluids, ambulation and minimal opioids. Flatus POD 6, stool POD 7; NG removed and diet advanced, tolerating a regular diet at discharge.

5. Diabetes - insulin sliding scale plus metformin. HTN - lisinopril continued. Enoxaparin for VTE prophylaxis while inpatient.

Discharge medications:
- Metformin 1000 mg twice daily
- Lisinopril 20 mg daily
- Aspirin 81 mg daily
- Amoxicillin-clavulanate 875/125 mg twice daily through 3/21 (NEW)

Allergies: NKDA.
Condition at discharge: stable, ambulating independently. Incision clean, staples to come out at the surgical follow-up.
Follow-up: surgery clinic 1-2 weeks; oncology; PCP within 1 week.

General Surgery

documents.title: Call from patient's wife
documents.author: RN
documents.body:
Mrs. Clark called to let the office know Carl was taken to the ED Saturday night with fever, belly pain and confusion and was admitted. She says there is "an infection in the blood" and the surgeons may do his colon operation while he's in. He is more himself this morning.

Offered support; asked her to call when he's discharged so we can see him within a week. Records request faxed to the hospital.

PCP notified.

documents.title: Transitional Care Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Post-hospital visit. Wife present. Discharge summary not yet received; history from patient, wife and his discharge paperwork.

Admitted 3/1-3/14: bloodstream infection (wife has the paperwork: "Clostridium septicum"), then right colon removed 3/5 during the same stay. Heart went into AF during and the morning after surgery, back to normal rhythm by 3/7, no new heart pills. Bowels slow to wake up afterwards, NG tube for a few days; now having BMs. Taking amoxicillin-clavulanate twice daily through Friday.

Today: tired but walking the house and the driveway. Eating small meals. No fever. No palpitations since discharge. Incision a little sore.

Meds reconciled: metformin 1000 BID, lisinopril 20, amlodipine 10 (on his own list at home; not on the hospital list), ASA 81, amox-clav to 3/21.

Exam: thin, NAD. Afebrile. Pulse regular. Heart RRR, S4, no murmur. Lungs clear. Midline incision with staples, clean, dry, no erythema or drainage. Abdomen soft, appropriately tender near incision, bowel sounds present. No calf tenderness or edema.

A/P:
1. Sepsis from C. septicum bacteremia - resolved; finishing oral course.
2. Metastatic ascending colon adenocarcinoma s/p open right hemicolectomy - surgical follow-up for staples next week; oncology to discuss chemotherapy.
3. Postoperative AF - resolved, regular today. Educated on palpitations; call if recurs.
4. Postoperative ileus - resolved.
5. T2DM - eating less; home fastings 100-130. Continue metformin for now.
6. HTN - BP fine on lisinopril + amlodipine.
BMP and CBC today. Will get the hospital records.

TCM, high complexity. 45 min.

documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT NOTE
DOS 04/05/2025 14:30
Carl Clark, 72 M

CC: right face swollen and painful.

HPI: Over two days his right cheek in front of the ear has become progressively swollen and painful. Since his colon surgery last month chewing has hurt and he has not been eating or drinking much. Background: metastatic colorectal cancer, right hemicolectomy last month, course complicated by atrial fibrillation and ileus. Also T2DM and HTN.

Meds: metformin 1000 mg BID, lisinopril 20 mg daily, aspirin 81 mg daily. NKDA.
SH: never smoker, no EtOH.

Vitals: T 38.6 C (101.5 F), BP 135/85, HR 98, RR 16.

Exam: Right parotid region swollen, red and tender. Massage of the gland expresses purulent material from Stensen's duct. No fluctuance. Floor of mouth soft. No stridor. Heart regular. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft; healing midline incision.

Labs: WBC 14,000 with 80% neutrophils. Glucose 180. Na 140, K 4.2, Cr 1.1.

Assessment: acute bacterial (suppurative) parotitis, right, in the setting of poor oral intake after surgery.

ED course: IV ampicillin-sulbactam 3 g, 1 L normal saline.

Disposition: home. Amoxicillin-clavulanate 875/125 mg BID x 10 days. Warm compresses, gland massage, sour candies or lemon drops to keep saliva flowing, plenty of fluids. Return for worsening swelling, trouble swallowing or breathing, or persistent fever. Follow up with PCP in 2-3 days.

Emergency Medicine

Day 3 of amoxicillin-clavulanate. Swelling down by about half, pain better, chewing soft foods. No fever since yesterday. Drinking 6-8 glasses a day now, sucking lemon drops. Staples out last week at surgery.

Exam: afebrile. R parotid region mildly swollen and tender, overlying redness fading. No fluctuance. No pus expressed from R Stensen's duct today. Oropharynx clear. No neck nodes enlarged beyond the gland. Heart regular. Lungs clear. Incision healed.

A/P:
1. Acute bacterial parotitis, right - improving. Complete 10 days. Hydration, warm compresses, massage, sialogogues. Call for worsening or new fever.
2. Metastatic colon cancer s/p resection - oncology visit 4/29 to plan chemo.
3. T2DM - glucose 180 in ED with infection; eating better now. Continue metformin.

RTC 2 weeks if not fully resolved, otherwise after oncology plan is set.

documents.title: Oncology Follow-up
documents.author: oncology
documents.body:
MEDICAL ONCOLOGY - FOLLOW-UP
Date of visit: 04/29/2025
Patient: Carl Clark

Interval: Admitted 3/1-3/14 with Clostridium septicum bacteremia; open right hemicolectomy 3/5 with pT3 pN1b moderately differentiated adenocarcinoma, margins negative. Course complicated by transient postoperative AF and ileus. ED visit 4/5 for right parotitis, treated with oral antibiotics and resolving. Recovering well, walking daily, appetite improving.

Staging CT 1/14/2025 (for the record): no thoracic metastases; liver lesions and ascending colon mass unchanged from November; no ascites or peritoneal disease.

Exam: ECOG 1. Healed midline incision. Liver edge palpable. No edema.

Assessment: Stage IV adenocarcinoma of the ascending colon, primary resected, bilobar liver metastases not resectable.

Plan:
1. FOLFOX (oxaliplatin, leucovorin, 5-fluorouracil) every 14 days, planned 12 cycles, with restaging CT every 3 months.
2. Implanted port placement by IR 5/6. Cycle 1 on 5/13.
3. Ondansetron 8 mg as needed for nausea.
4. Chemotherapy teaching completed today with patient and wife.

Allergies: NKDA.
Medical Oncology

medications.sig: IV bolus and 46-hour infusion every 14 days per oncology
Take 1 tablet by mouth every 8 hours as needed for nausea

documents.title: started chemo
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Got the port put in on the 6th and had my first chemo last Tuesday. They sent me home with the pump for 2 days. Not too bad, a little queasy, used the nausea pill twice. The cheek is all better. Question - do I keep taking the metformin on chemo days? The oncology nurse said ask you.

documents.title: RE: started chemo
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Glad the first round went OK and the parotid infection has cleared. Yes, keep taking metformin. If you are not able to eat on a given day, or you are vomiting, skip that day's doses and call us. Check your sugar a few times a week and let me know if you see readings under 80 or over 250. I've added the chemo drugs to your list here so our records match oncology's.

AWV.

On FOLFOX since May, cycle 10 last week. Tolerating without dose changes. Walking about 20 min most days. Independent in ADLs; wife drives him to infusions. No falls. PHQ-2 0; enjoying time at home, sleeping fine.

Per patient, August CT showed shrinkage; oncology note requested, not received.

Advance care planning: wife remains HCP. He has thought about what he would want if very ill; plans to talk it over with oncology and his wife. Will revisit.

reports.text:
Comparison: 08/12/2025 and 01/14/2025.
Interval decrease in size of multiple hypoattenuating liver lesions in both lobes; largest now 2.3 cm in the right lobe (2.9 cm in August, 4.6 cm at baseline). No new hepatic lesions. reports.conclusion: Continued partial response of hepatic metastases, largest 2.3 cm. No new disease.

documents.title: Oncology Follow-up
documents.author: oncology
documents.body:
MEDICAL ONCOLOGY - FOLLOW-UP
Visit 10/28/2025
Carl Clark, 73 M. Stage IV adenocarcinoma of the ascending colon, liver metastases, s/p right hemicolectomy 3/2025.

Treatment: FOLFOX q14 days, cycles 1-12, 5/13/2025 to 10/14/2025, completed without dose modification.

Response: restaging CT 8/12/2025 showed partial response, liver lesions smaller, largest 2.9 cm (4.6 cm at baseline), no new disease; CEA 11.4. CT today: further decrease, largest 2.3 cm, no new disease. CEA today 5.9 ng/mL (46.2 at diagnosis).

Tolerating treatment. ECOG 1.

Plan:
1. Oxaliplatin stopped after 12 planned cycles.
2. Maintenance 5-FU/leucovorin every 2 weeks beginning 11/11/2025.
3. Restage with CT and CEA in the spring.

Allergies: NKDA.
Medical Oncology
